dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product names things from code inside its sentences — a command, a file, a property, a value to type — in its help, its settings, its error messages and its release notes, and wants each told from the words around it at a glance, on the same line and at the size of the text it sits in.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything inline code reads: the fill behind it, its corners, the room on each side of the text and an edge a layer may give it; the text's color and face; and how large the code face is drawn beside the text it sits in.
rules: Inline code is a run of text in a sentence: a command, a name, a value. More than one line of code, or code people will copy whole, is a code block.
Keys to press are a keyboard shortcut, never inline code.
It takes the size of the text it sits in: never set a font size on it. In a heading it is the heading's size.

Use variant plain where every cell of a column or every item of a list is code, and on a colored container (a callout, an inverse surface): the face alone tells it there, and it takes the color of the text around it.
Inline code is never highlighted and never a control. A name that leads somewhere is a link that holds inline code.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never draw the fill by hand.

color.$description: The fill behind the text in the tonal form: the faintest fill that still reads as a shape on the surfaces text sits on, the one a key cap takes. Decorative: the face tells code from words where the fill cannot be seen (on a container of the same tone, in forced colors). The plain form draws none.

shape.$description: The fill's corners, on every piece of a run that breaks across lines.

padding-inline.$description: Room between the fill's edge and the text, at the start and the end of every piece of a run. It is drawn, not typed: copying the text copies no space for it.

color.$description: The edge of the fill where a layer gives it a width: the system's one hairline. Decorative.

width.$description: The width of an edge around the fill, drawn inside it. Nothing in the default system: a fill or a line, not both. A layer that draws its inline code outlined sets it (sys.border.hairline).

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product draws its inline code as a faint fill; another, whose surfaces are already tinted, as an outlined box.

color.$description: The text's color in the tonal form, read on container.color. Inside a link the text takes the link's color in its place. The plain form takes the color of the text around it and reads no token.

typescale.$description: The face: the family, weight and letter spacing of the code role. Its size and line height are not taken: the size is the surrounding text's by label.scale, and inline code never sets a line's height.

scale.$description: How large the code face is drawn, as a fraction of the font size of the text it sits in: in body text it is the code role's own size, and in a heading, a lead paragraph or a caption it keeps the same proportion. 1 draws both faces at one size.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A ratio between the apparent sizes of two faces (the code role's 13 beside the body role's 14), not a distance: the type dials scale both sizes alike, so no dial moves it.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product pairs a text face and a code face whose letters do not look the same size at the same font size, and evens them out once for every place code appears in a sentence.
